oil.summary: Crude markets posted a sharp intraday divergence: WTI gained 1.54% to $90.75/bbl while Brent shed 4.15% to $98.30/bbl, the spread widening materially against a backdrop of extreme geopolitical noise. The Hormuz crisis remains the dominant macro driver — oil touched $103 intraday per live headlines — but price action has turned two-way as China demand concerns weigh. Analysts cut Q4 Chinese import forecasts by 400,000 bpd, citing price resistance above $100. The EIA reported a 900,000-barrel crude build, though diesel stocks sitting 14% below seasonal average provided a floor. Russia extended its diesel export ban through October 31, tightening distillate markets further. OPEC+ is widely expected to hold quotas unchanged at this weekend's meeting, and the Dallas Fed survey confirmed U.S. production continues to climb despite WTI's $67-to-$107 swing inside three months.
drivers: Hormuz crisis sustaining geopolitical risk premium; analysts raise 2026 price forecasts as disruption drags on
China Q4 import forecasts cut 400k bpd and EIA crude build cap topside, creating Brent/WTI spread volatility
Russia extends diesel export ban through Oct. 31, deepening distillate tightness with stocks already 14% below average

gas.summary: Natural gas price action was constructive on both sides of the Atlantic. Henry Hub edged up 0.43% to $3.024/MMBtu, holding a modest monthly gain of just over 3%. TTF outperformed with a 3.29% single-day surge to €72.105/MWh — matching its full monthly gain in one session — as the German government ordered state-owned SEFE to add 8 TWh to storage, signalling official concern over winter adequacy. U.S. production continues to climb per the Dallas Fed Q3 survey, which should limit Henry Hub upside, but European supply anxiety is clearly re-pricing TTF. Note: headline coverage for this sector today is thin beyond these three items; further nuance is limited to available data.
drivers: Germany mandates SEFE to inject 8 TWh into storage, signalling winter supply anxiety and lifting TTF 3.29% on the day
U.S. gas production rising per Dallas Fed Q3 survey, capping Henry Hub despite broader energy risk-on environment
Broader energy inflation shock in Europe — amplified by oil market tightness — adding upward pressure to TTF

power.summary: EU carbon (EUA) slipped 1.20% to $80.945/EUA and is down 1.89% on the week, even as TTF surged 3.29% on the day — a divergence suggesting near-term carbon demand expectations are not keeping pace with gas price stress. Europe is absorbing another energy-driven inflation shock, with accelerating CPI across major euro-area economies per today's reports. A deadly explosion at one of India's largest refineries adds peripheral fuel-supply risk, though its direct EUA impact is limited. Trump's denial of Iran sanctions relief and ongoing Hormuz disruption are the key geopolitical inputs sustaining the broader energy complex, but power-specific headline flow today is sparse; the carbon softness amid rising gas prices may reflect short-term compliance selling into quarter-end.
drivers: EUA falls 1.20% on likely quarter-end compliance selling despite supportive gas price backdrop
Europe facing accelerating energy-driven inflation with ECB policy room constrained, per today's reporting
Indian refinery explosion tightens regional fuel supply; Hormuz disruption sustains geopolitical risk premium across the energy complex
